title: SiNx ARC Conversion to Sodium Silicate

key_findings.detail:
The conversion of SiNx to sodium silicate occurs under basic conditions generated by leakage current:

- Hydroxide ions (OH⁻) are generated at the front glass surface or EVA interface under the applied electric field
- In the basic environment (high [OH⁻]), SiNxOy is attacked at gridline contact points where the local pH is highest
- **Primary reaction:** SiNxOy + 2OH⁻ + (1−y)H₂O → (SiO₃)²⁻ + xNH₃ + H₂

- [[papers/Wiley-136-1282-2-s2.0-85148423463-2023-J-Electrochemical mechanisms of leakage-current in photovoltaic modules.pdf#page=5|Vogt et al. (2023), p.5]]

Na₂SiO₃ formation is concentrated at:

- **Gridline contact points:** Where negative bias creates the highest local field and where metallic contacts catalyze the electrochemical reaction
- These sites serve as nucleation points for the chemical attack
- [[papers/Wiley-136-1282-2-s2.0-85148423463-2023-J-Electrochemical mechanisms of leakage-current in photovoltaic modules.pdf#page=6|Vogt et al. (2023), p.6]]

The ARC acts as a large capacitor during the early stages of voltage application:

- ARC capacitance: **~570 nF** (orders of magnitude larger than polymer capacitance of ~0.11 nF)
- Charge buildup at the polymer-to-SiNxOy interface creates complex discharge behavior with multiple time constants
  - Long: > 0.4 h
  - Medium: 0.1–0.4 h
  - Short: < 0.1 h
- Multiple charge carrier species with different diffusion rates exist at this interface (at least 2–3 species)
- [[papers/Wiley-136-1282-2-s2.0-85148423463-2023-J-Electrochemical mechanisms of leakage-current in photovoltaic modules.pdf#page=3|Vogt et al. (2023), p.3]]

Conversion of SiNx to sodium silicate:

- Disrupts the dense SiNx matrix that otherwise acts as an effective Na⁺ diffusion barrier
- Creates locally porous or compositionally altered regions through which Na⁺ can more easily diffuse to the Si cell
- Compounds the PID mechanism by reducing the effectiveness of the ARC as a protective layer
- [[papers/Wiley-136-1282-2-s2.0-85148423463-2023-J-Electrochemical mechanisms of leakage-current in photovoltaic modules.pdf#page=7|Vogt et al. (2023), p.7]]

After prolonged voltage exposure, the glass surface develops a Na⁺-depleted layer:

- After voltage exposure, glass surface resistance increases by a factor of **~2.9** due to depletion of surface charge carriers
- The depletion zone is a more pure SiO₂-like layer with increased resistivity
- This is a **self-limiting** process that partially reduces leakage current over very long timescales
- [[papers/Wiley-136-1282-2-s2.0-85148423463-2023-J-Electrochemical mechanisms of leakage-current in photovoltaic modules.pdf#page=4|Vogt et al. (2023), p.4]]
